items.question: In your own words, briefly describe what makes you the ideal candidate for this position.
items.problem:
Expected "I build data systems that have to hold up against real data and real users, not just a notebook. On a Gates Foundation-funded Johns Hopkins and South African Medical Research Council health equity project, I was lead model developer: I trained XGBoost models on a national survey dataset of roughly 10 million records to identify drivers of multimorbidity, used SHAP for feature selection and interpretation, and designed G-formula causal simulations to estimate counterfactual intervention outcomes. That work required constant back and forth with the principal investigator about variable selection and specification, so I got used to translating statistics into questions a non-modeler actually cares about.

At Intelehealth I built a resource-availability scoring pipeline in Python across 32 villages combining facility-tier classification, geospatial distance, Maps and weather data, and I designed an evaluation framework using stratified sampling to compare AI-generated clinical outputs against a 4,169-case clinical standard and surface systematic failure modes. Currently I build the machine learning core of an anomaly-detection and alert-prioritization system, including the ingestion pipeline and a FastAPI detection service.

I am comfortable owning a piece of a system end to end and documenting it well enough that someone else can trust the output."; page shows "(empty)"
